title: killall
definition: A command that kills processes by their exact name, rather than their numeric Process ID (PID). It sends a signal to every single process sharing that name.
simpleExplanation: The shotgun. Instead of looking up 5 different ID numbers to kill 5 Python scripts, you just say 'Kill everything named Python'.
realWorldExample: You accidentally started 10 background instances of the `nginx` web server. Finding and killing all 10 PIDs manually would take forever. You type `killall nginx`, and all 10 are terminated instantly.

basic: What happens if you type `killall python` but accidentally spell it `killall pyhton`?
intermediate: Why is running `killall` generally considered dangerous on a shared production server?

answers.question: Misspell name?
answers.answer: It will simply output 'no process found' and do nothing.

answers.question: Why dangerous?
answers.answer: Because it doesn't ask questions. If you type `killall node`, it will kill YOUR node app, but it will also kill the production node app being run by the database team, bringing down the entire company's website.
